content.title: About
content.content: Triscuit crackers are crunchy baked wheat wafers formed into a woven pattern. They have a light salty flavor and a distinctive airy texture. The product is often enjoyed as a snack on its own or paired with cheese, spreads, and soups.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Triscuit was first introduced in the United States in 1901 under the name "Triscuit" (derived from "tri" — three and "scuit" — biscuit).
Traditionally they are made from whole wheat kernels without refined flour.
The woven shape is created by a special pressing process that forms the characteristic grid‑like holes.
The original recipe uses only wheat, vegetable oil, salt, and a small amount of sugar.
Triscuit crackers are frequently used in recipes as a base for canapé‑style appetizers.

items.title: Source of whole grains
items.content: Whole‑grain wheat provides fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals that support healthy digestion.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: Unlike many sweet snacks, Triscuit contains virtually no added sugar, making it a more moderate choice.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: Each serving supplies a modest amount of plant‑based protein, beneficial for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: Fiber and complex carbohydrates help keep you feeling full longer after eating.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: The manufacturing process does not use hydrogenated oils, reducing trans‑fat content.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with gluten intolerance or wheat allergy may experience adverse reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Crackers are lightly salted; individuals limiting sodium should monitor portion size.

items.title: Moderate glycemic index
items.content: Despite whole grains, the carbohydrate profile can raise blood sugar levels in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Triscuit crackers can be eaten straight from the bag, topped with cream cheese, hummus, avocado, or used as a base for mini‑sandwiches. They pair well with soups and salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in the original packaging or an airtight container. For extended shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to maintain crispness.
